topic: Processor Pipelining and Hazard Handling (illustrated through x86-64 Assembly Optimization)
explanation: Modern processors employ pipelining to execute instructions concurrently, increasing performance. However, dependencies between instructions (hazards) can stall the pipeline. Optimizing assembly code minimizes these hazards for improved performance. This is crucial for systems programming where performance is paramount.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)

book: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
code_example:
; Pipelining: Data Hazard (RAW) Mitigation
; Load/Use dependencies cause stalls (5-cycle latency common)

; --- Stalled Sequence Example ---
mov r10, [rdi]    ; Load R10 (Latency begins)
inc r10           ; RAW Hazard: Pipeline stalls
mov [rsi], r10    ; Store

; --- Instruction Scheduled (Optimized) ---
mov r10, [rdi]    ; Load R10
mov r11, [r8]     ; Independent instruction 1 (Fills delay slot)
add r11, 42       ; Independent instruction 2
inc r10           ; R10 ready; Stall avoided
mov [rsi], r10    ; Store result

; Avoid long dependency chains for better throughput.
keywords: Instruction Pipeline, Pipeline Hazard, Assembly Optimization, Data Hazard
